O=C(O)c1c[nH]c2c(F)cc(I)cc2c1=O

c1c[nH]c2...c1=O -> c1 is part of a ring.
Let's draw it out mentally or use a tool if available, but I'll just parse SMILES.
Ring 1: c1 ... c1=O. It contains [nH], and two carbonyls attached to it?

C(=O)O attached to c1.
c1 is connected to c (which is connected to [nH]), which is connected to c2.
c2 is connected to c(F), c, c(I), c, c, which connects back to c1=O.
So it's a fused bicyclic system: a 5-membered ring containing [nH] and a 6-membered ring.
Wait, c1c[nH]c2...c1=O. The 5-membered ring has c1, c, [nH], c2, and another atom?
Let's count atoms in the 5-membered ring: c1 - c - [nH] - c2 - ? - c1. Wait, c1 is connected to c1=O. So the 5-membered ring is c1-c-[nH]-c2-C(=O)-c1? That would be an imidazolone.
Actually, O=C(O)c1c[nH]c2c(F)cc(I)cc2c1=O
Let's break it down:
O=C(O)-C1=C(C(=O))-N(H)-C2=C(F)-C=C(I)-C=C2-1
Wait, c1c[nH]c2c(F)cc(I)cc2c1=O
If we expand:
O=C(O)c1c[nH]c2c(F)cc(I)cc2c1=O
Atom 1: C(=O)O attached to C1
C1 is double bonded to C (let's call it C3)
C3 is single bonded to N(H)
N(H) is single bonded to C2
C2 is double bonded to C(F)
C(F) is single bonded to C
C is single bonded to C(I)
C(I) is single bonded to C
C is single bonded to C(=O) which is attached to C1.
So the 5-membered ring is C1-C3-N(H)-C2-C(=O)-C1. This is an imidazol-4-one (or 5-one) ring. Specifically, it's a 4-oxo-4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole-2-carboxylic acid derivative? Wait, numbering: N1-C2(=O)-C3(=C(O)O)-N4(H)-C5(=C2)-...
Actually, it's a uracil-like or imidazolone fused to a benzene ring? No, c2c(F)cc(I)cc2 is a benzene ring!
So it's a benzimidazolone derivative!
Specifically, 5-fluoro-7-iodo-2-oxo-2,3-dihydro-1H-benzimidazole-4-carboxylic acid? Or 4-fluoro-6-iodo...
Let's check the positions:
Benzene ring: c2c(F)cc(I)cc2. F is at position adjacent to fusion, I is at meta to F.
Fused imidazolone: c1c[nH]c2...c1=O.
